Dear All.

I am trying to run this model below where all the covariates are assumed to have  linear effects on the response except age (non-linear), which I am smoothing using a RW2  model.{ f(age,model="rw2")} and CountyX which is the county id (unstructured).

formula<-HIV~educationlevel+age_first_sex+perceived_Risk+partners_last_1yr+Urban+Freq_of_travel_away+MaritalStatusX+STI+f(age,model="rw2")+f(countyX, model="iid")

The problem is that I only obtain a smooth curve when I fit and plot the fitted mean against age when I only include age in my model. i.e:

formula<-HIV~ f(age,model="rw2")

resultt<-inla(formula,family="binomial",data=ken_data,control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,mlik=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

dd<-resultt$summary.fitted.values

plot(age,dd[,4])---- dd[,4] is the 0.5 quant

 

Figure1

When I add one more covariate say, education level which has 4 categories but the first is the reference category:

formula<-HIV~ f(age,model="rw2")+ educationlevel.

result0<-inla(formula,family="binomial",data=ken_data,control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,mlik=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

dd<-resultt$summary.fitted.values

plot(age,dd[,4])----dd[,4] is the 0.5 quant

 I get:

Figure 2

And so on eventually when I  include all the covariates:

formula<-HIV~educationlevel+age_first_sex+perceived_Risk+partners_last_1yr+Urban+Freq_of_travel_away+MaritalStatusX+STI+f(age,model="rw2")+f(countyX, model="iid")

result0<-inla(formula,family="binomial",data=ken_data,control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,mlik=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

dd<-result0$summary.fitted.values

plot(age,dd[,4])--- ----dd[,4] is the 0.5 quant

and try to obtain a smooth curve for age alone I get:

Is it my model or what? How do I obtain the smooth curve as in Figure 1, even after including all the variables.

Many Thanks.
